h.t: Install on Linux and Steam Deck

x: MajesticTab runs on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, Android, Linux and Steam Deck. After you install it, it works offline. Direct downloads are on the latest release page . Install on iPhone and iPad Get MajesticTab from the App Store. One purchase unlocks the app on iPhone, iPad and Mac. If you would rather not use the App Store, you have two options: Build it yourself. MajesticTab is open source. The build steps for iOS are in CONTRIBUTING.md . You need a Mac with Xcode, and you sign the app for your own device with your own Apple ID. Use the web app at majestictab.zathu.net/app . In Safari, choose Share, then Add to Home Screen. The web app has fewer features than the app: Browser storage is temporary. Your system can clear tabs and map points saved in the browser when storage is low or browsing data is cleared. The app has permanent offline storage. No local Jam hosting. No secure credential store. No iCloud sync for Apple devices. Install on Mac Choose one of these: Get MajesticTab from the Mac App Store. It's the same purchase as the iPhone and iPad app. Download a free .dmg file from the release page. There is one for Apple silicon and one for Intel Macs. Install on Windows Choose one of these: Get MajesticTab from the Microsoft Store. It's free. Download the installer ( .exe ) from the release page. There is one for x86_64 PCs and one for ARM64 PCs. Install on Android Choose one of these: Get MajesticTab from Google Play. It's free. Download the .apk file from the release page and open it. F-Droid isn't available yet. Install on Linux and Steam Deck MajesticTab is a Flatpak for x86_64 and ARM64. The easiest way to install it, and to get updates, is the Zathu Flatpak repository. To add it, follow these steps: Download zathu.flatpakrepo . Open the file with KDE Discover or GNOME Software, and then confirm that you want to add the Zathu Software source. Search for MajesticTab and install it. To use a terminal instead, run the following commands: The first install also downloads the GNOME runtime from Flathub. Your software center, or flatpak update , then keeps MajesticTab up to date. You can also install a single file. Download the file for your processor from the release page. Then run the following command. Replace FILE with the name of the file you downloaded. A file you install this way doesn't update itself: On a Steam Deck, run the command in Desktop Mode. MajesticTab supports the Deck's controls. See Foot pedals and game controllers . Update the app Store versions update through the store. Versions that update themselves have an Updates section in Settings. To check for an update, follow these steps: Select Settings in the library navigation and then select Updates . Under Update channel , choose Stable , Canary or None . Next to Check for updates , select Check . Cost MajesticTab is open source. It's free on the Microsoft Store, Google Play, Linux and direct downloads. On the Apple App Store, a one-time purchase unlocks the app on iPhone, iPad and Mac. MajesticTab has no subscriptions, ads or accounts.

h.t: Add a tab to your library

x: This page shows you how to play a tab and add it to your library. Play a tab In this guide, select means click with a mouse or tap on a touch screen. Where an action also works from a keyboard or a game controller, the guide says so. Select Open a single file . This plays a tab without adding it to your library. You find it on the start screen. After your library has songs, the start screen no longer appears. Then select Tools in the library views at the top of the Library, and select Open file . Choose a Guitar Pro file ( .gp , .gp3 to .gp5 or .gpx ), a PDF or a text tab. To play, select Play / Pause in the playback dock, press Space , or press A on a game controller. Use the same control again to pause. A Guitar Pro tab plays through the built-in synth, and the cursor follows the music. If a PDF or text tab has no audio loaded, Space turns the page. You can also turn pages by selecting Next page or Previous page in the top bar, selecting the right or left half of the page, pressing the arrow keys, or pressing RB or LB on a game controller. The reader shows the score, the five controls and the playback dock. Add a tab to your library Open the Library . In the search field at the top, type the name of a song, an artist or an album. MajesticTab searches the music catalog and fills in the artist, cover, year and track order. To add an album, select the album and then select Add album . To add one song, select Add song next to a track in the album's tracklist. On the song, select Add tab and choose your file. If the catalog doesn't list your music, type its name and select Add song on the result Add "your text" as a custom song . If you already opened the tab, open the song menu and select Save to library . Learn the reader controls The reader groups its controls under five words: View , Practice , Sound , Guitar and Tools . To slow a part down and repeat it, start with Practice . The reader describes all five. Next steps Organize your library Map a tab to the original recording Look up keyboard shortcuts

h.t: Link a tab to a song

x: The library organizes tabs by song. Each song has an artist, an album and a place in the album's tracklist. You can link several tabs to one song. An artist in the library, with albums, tracklists and linked tabs. Add songs, albums and books You can add music in these ways: Search the catalog. Type a song, artist or album in the search field at the top of the Library. MajesticTab fetches the artist's discography, album covers, release years and track orders, so your songs match the real releases. Select Add album to add an album with its tracklist, or select Add song next to a track to add that song. Add custom music. If the catalog doesn't list your music, type its name in the search field and select Add song on the result Add "your text" as a custom song . In an empty library, you can also select Add custom music on the start screen. Add a book. Open an album, select Add book and choose where the PDF comes from. See PDF and text tabs . If MajesticTab can't reach the catalog, you see Unable to reach music catalog . You can still add custom music. Link a tab to a song A song without a tab shows No tab yet . To link a Guitar Pro, PDF or text file, select Add tab . To search the web for a tab, select Find tab . See Getting tabs in . A song can have several tabs. MajesticTab reopens the last tab you used. Type a tab as text To write a tab or lyrics yourself, select Add tab , or Add another tab on a song that has tabs, then select Enter as text . MajesticTab adds an empty text tab to the song and opens it with the Edit text window. Type or paste your text and select Save . The tab opens like any other text tab. To change the text later, open the tab, open the Song menu and select Edit text . If you close the window before you save anything, it opens again the next time you open the tab. Browse and search The library views at the top let you switch between Library , Setlists , Tools and Tunings . To find a song, type in the search field. It filters songs that have tabs as you type. Pin songs and artists Pin a song or an artist to keep it easy to reach. Pinned songs show in Pinned songs . Reopen recent tabs Recently opened lists the tabs you opened last. To remove entries, select Edit recents list . To remove all entries, select Clear history . Rename or remove a song Use Rename to change a song's name. Use Remove from library to take a song out of the library. In the web version, your browser controls how long it keeps your data. Back up your library before you rely on it.

A setlist lists songs in the order you plan to play them. Tuning groups organize the library by how you tune. Create a setlist In the library views, select Setlists . Select New setlist and enter a name. Search for songs and add them. You can also select Add to setlist on a song. Edit a setlist Select Edit setlist . Then you can move songs up or down and remove them. To delete the whole setlist, select Delete setlist . Play a setlist Select Start set to open the first tab. While the setlist is open, select Previous in setlist or Next in setlist in the top bar. These buttons show your position, for example 2/8. On a keyboard, press [ for the previous tab and ] for the next tab. Browse by tuning The library grouped by tuning. Every song records its tuning. In the library views, select Tunings to group your library by Standard, Drop D, D Standard, DADGAD, 7-string, 8-string or a custom tuning. Choose songs from one group to play a set without retuning.

h.t: Open files from your cloud storage
Search the web for a tab
Fill in tabs for songs that have none

x: You choose where your tabs come from. Files stay on your device unless you back them up or sync them. Open files from your device MajesticTab opens Guitar Pro files ( .gp , .gp3 to .gp5 , .gpx ), PDFs and text tabs. To link a file to a song, select Add tab . To play a file without adding it to your library, select Open file under Tools in the library views. On the start screen of an empty library, the same action is called Open a single file . See Open file . Open files from your cloud storage Connect Google Drive, S3, WebDAV or iCloud to browse folders and open scores on any of your devices. Connecting is optional. You use your own account. You can also use these connections to sync your library . Search the web for a tab On a song, select Find tab . In the search that opens, find a Guitar Pro, PDF or text file and download it. If the file does not open in MajesticTab on its own, select Add tab on the song and choose the file. Searching the web needs an internet connection. To change the search site, see Settings . Fill in tabs for songs that have none To search the web for a tab of each song that has none, select Tools in the library views and select Fill in missing tabs . See Fill in missing tabs . Import a folder To add many files at once, select Bulk import a folder of tabs on the start screen. After your library has songs, the start screen no longer appears. Then select Tools in the library views and select Bulk import . See Bulk import . Browse classical tabs To browse classical guitar tabs and MIDI files, select Explore classical guitar library on the start screen. After your library has songs, select Tools in the library views and select Classical tab browser . You download the archive when you first use it. MajesticTab doesn't include it. See Classical tab browser . Restore a backup To load a .mtbackup file, open Settings , select Data management and select Restore next to Restore from a backup . On the start screen, you can also select Restore a backup . See Backup and sync .

Your library is stored on your device. You can save a copy to one file, or keep your devices in sync through cloud storage that you own. Back up your library Select Settings in the library navigation and then select Data management . Next to Create a backup , select Create . Check the file name, then select Back up . The backup is one .mtbackup file that MajesticTab saves on your device. To save it somewhere else, such as Google Drive, an S3 bucket or a WebDAV server, select Save somewhere else before you select Back up . The screen also shows when you last made a backup on this device. The file holds your library, setlists, settings and SoundFonts. Each song is stored as a standard .mpak file inside it, with its tabs, the recordings you saved with it and their map points. A backup is a standalone copy, good to keep before you change anything large. Restore a backup In Data management , next to Restore from a backup , select Restore . On the start screen of an empty library, you can also select Restore a backup . Choose a .mtbackup file (in the web app and on Mac and Windows you can also drop one on the screen). MajesticTab shows how many songs, setlists and SoundFonts it holds and when it was made. Choose how to restore it, then select Restore backup : Add missing items keeps everything you have and adds what the backup has and you lack. Songs that are already in your library are left as they are. Replace all data erases your stored tabs, library, settings and audio files first, and replaces them with the backup. Tick the box to confirm. If a file is damaged or incomplete, MajesticTab restores what it can and tells you how many files were missing. Backups made by earlier versions of MajesticTab still restore. Snapshots that an earlier version saved to Google Drive, an S3 bucket, a WebDAV server or a backup folder are on the same screen, under the file picker. Sync your library across devices In Cloud sync under Cloud storage , next to Sync with cloud storage , select Sync and choose one of these locations: Google Drive iCloud Drive S3 bucket WebDAV server A folder on this device MajesticTab compares this device with the sync location and lists what it will receive, send, combine or remove. Select Sync now to apply the changes. Songs, recordings, collections, recents, setlists, SoundFonts, pins, web search sources and your chosen videos and recordings stay in step across your devices. Other settings, such as the instrument, strings and SoundFont choices, stay on each device; a backup file still holds them. By default, sync keeps your song list in step while leaving files in your sync location until you open a song (pinned songs and songs in setlists still download right away). Turn on Keep all files on device before syncing to download every song in your library onto this device. To clear copies already on this device when keeping files in the cloud, select Remove local files already in Drive (or your sync location). To overwrite the sync location with what is on this device, select the Replace action in the sync header (such as Replace Drive or Replace bucket ) and confirm. This sends everything from this device and removes anything in the sync location that isn't on this device. Turn on Auto-sync cloud storage to keep your library synced in the background whenever a location is connected. While a background sync runs, a thin progress bar appears along the top edge of the app alongside a brief notification when it starts. If auto-sync pauses for sign-in, folder access or review, a notification lets you open Sync directly; while you are playing or in Reading mode, notifications wait until you stop. MajesticTab uses your own account or folder. Sync is optional. Export your library To export your library as a spreadsheet, your map points, your original tab files or printable PDFs, select Tools in the library views and then select Bulk export . See Bulk export . To export one tab as a PDF, open the song menu and select Export as PDF . Manage stored data Data management also contains these rows: Reload library metadata refreshes covers, durations and album details. Orphaned files finds stored tabs that no library song uses. Clear cached data clears covers and downloads that MajesticTab keeps only to load faster. Delete all data removes your library, setlists and settings from this device. Make a backup first. In the web version, the browser stores your data and can clear it. MajesticTab warns you that browser storage is temporary. Make backups, or use cloud sync.

h.t: Turn pages and move the cursor
Hide the controls with Reading mode
Use the reader on a phone

x: The reader has five controls and one playback dock. The controls use the same names on every platform. In this guide, select means click with a mouse or tap on a touch screen. Where an action also works from a keyboard or a game controller, the guide gives those ways too. The reader with the Practice panel open. Use the five controls View Layout, notation, size, paper, the pages shown, and which tracks are drawn. Practice Speed, parts, the loop range, the metronome and the count-in. Sound The settings for the sound you selected in the dock, either the synth or the original recording. Guitar Strings, tuning and capo for your guitar. Tools Chord library, scales, circle of fifths, tuner, metronome and Jam. Open the song menu Select the song name in the top bar to open the song menu. It contains these items: Pin , Save to library and Add to setlist For PDFs, Condense PDF and Bookmarks Export source tab , Export song file (.mpak) , Share original file , Share as song file (.mpak) and Export as PDF Use the dock The dock contains the playback controls, the Synth and Original switch, the volume control and a button for the fretboard . The switch only chooses which sound you hear. If you select Original before you add a recording, its settings open so you can add one. Move through a song with the bar ruler On a Guitar Pro tab, the bar ruler shows the whole song as one strip. It divides the song into sections, such as verse, chorus and solo, and shows a name on each section that has room for one. To move the playhead, select a point on the ruler or drag along it. When the ruler has focus, you can also use the arrow keys. While you move the playhead, a readout shows the section and bar. PDF and text tabs have a page strip instead. Turn pages and move the cursor In page mode, select the right half of the score for the next page and the left half for the previous page, or select Next page or Previous page in the top bar. On a touch screen, you can also swipe left for the next page and right for the previous page. On a keyboard, press the arrow keys, Page Up or Page Down . On a game controller, press RB or LB . A foot pedal that sends arrow keys also works. In scroll mode, the score scrolls. Use the mouse wheel, a swipe, the arrow keys or the left stick on a game controller. Select a beat to move the cursor to it. On a phone, use the bar ruler to move the cursor. To zoom between 50% and 150%, pinch on a touch screen or trackpad, hold Ctrl and use the mouse wheel, or push the right stick on a game controller. Hide the controls with Reading mode To hide the top bar and the controls, select Reading mode in the dock, press R , or press Y on a game controller. On desktop, Reading mode is also under Screen in the View panel. Only play and pause, the progress track and the Reading mode button remain. Nothing hides on its own. Scrolling, timers, taps and playback leave the controls where they are. To show everything again, use the same control again. Use the reader on a phone In portrait, the top bar is one slim row with the back button, the song name and the page buttons. The five controls are at the bottom, above the playback strip. In landscape, the five controls move to a rail.

View controls how the score looks: its layout, its notation, its size, its paper and which tracks it shows. The View panel. Choose a layout Select Page for book-like pages or Scroll for one continuous score. In landscape, you can show as many pages as fit, or one page. You can also choose whether a page turn moves one page or the whole view. View changes these options for the song you have open. To set the usual layout for each file type, use A new tab opens as under Reading in Settings . Choose notation Select Tab Only or Tab + Standard . Set the size and paper To zoom the score between 50% and 150%, use the size control, pinch on a touch screen or trackpad, hold Ctrl and use the mouse wheel, or push the right stick on a game controller. The paper can be Auto , Light or Dark . Choose which tracks to show Two guitar tracks drawn together. When a file has more than one track, View lists the tracks. MajesticTab stacks the guitar tracks on the page and keeps drums, bass, keys and vocals out of the way. It remembers your choice for each file. Show all draws every track. Color by track gives each track its own color in the score and on the fretboard. Change the theme MajesticTab has nine app themes. Each theme has a light or dark sheet. To change the theme, open Settings and select Appearance . See Settings .

Practice contains the controls for learning a part slowly and bringing it up to tempo. Change the speed Set the playback speed from 50% to 125%. Select a preset (50%, 75%, 90%, 100%, 110% or 125%) or use the buttons to change the speed in steps of 1%. On a keyboard, press , to slow down and . to speed up, in steps of 5%. The pitch stays the same. This includes a local audio file that you linked as the original recording. Loop bars You can repeat part of a song in two ways: Under Sections , select a section to loop it. Under Loop bars , enter a From bar and a To bar . Use the metronome and count-in To turn on the metronome and the count-in, select the Metronome and Count-in switches in Practice. You can also press M and I . When you map the original recording, the metronome and count-in follow it through tempo changes. Choose the parts to play Under Audio Tracks , select Full Band , Guitars Only or No Guitars . No Guitars plays the other instruments so you can play the guitar part yourself. To switch between full band and no guitars from a keyboard, press G . In bass mode, the same key switches between full band and no bass. Rewind To go back 10 seconds, select Back 10 Seconds in the dock, press B , or press X on a game controller.

Sound opens the settings for the sound you selected in the dock. Select Synth for MajesticTab's built-in playback, or Original for a recording. Use the synth MajesticTab plays Guitar Pro tabs through a built-in SoundFont synth that works offline. Mix the tracks The Mixer sets the volume and pan of each track, and lets you mute or solo it. Select Reset levels to return every track to its default. Add SoundFonts Open SoundFonts to add your own .sf2 or .sf3 files. You can also manage them in Settings under Sound . Backups include your SoundFonts. Use the original recording Select Original in the dock to play a YouTube video or an audio file instead of the synth. The cursor follows the recording. See Original recording . Compensate for audio latency A Bluetooth speaker can play sound late. Audio latency delays the cursor, scrolling and fretboard to match. Use -10 and +10 to change the compensation in steps of 10 ms, or select Calibrate to measure it. To calibrate, start the clicks and tap each time you hear a click. After a few taps, MajesticTab shows the measured delay. Select Apply to use it. Play bass tabs If you play bass, set Preferred instrument to Bass under Player in Settings .

h.t: Use a recording in a Jam

x: Map a tab to a recording, and the cursor follows the music. You can use a YouTube video or an audio file on your device. The original recording panel. Add a recording In the dock, select Original . If you haven't added a recording, its settings open. For an audio file on your device, select Add audio file and choose the file. For YouTube, enter a link or video ID under Add a video , or search by song. A link or ID is added as you entered it. A search adds the first match. Select Add to Full band or Add to Backing to choose where the video goes and add it. The list Recordings for this tab shows everything you added: audio files, then videos. A Guitar Pro file that carries its own audio adds a row at the top, Audio in the Guitar Pro file . When the recordings came from a song pack, each is listed by what the pack says it is: the original first, then alternate versions, then other kinds such as live, then backing tracks. The pack's own name for a recording is its title, and a backing track made without a part says so (for example, Without Drums). A part split from a mix sits under that mix. Recordings you added yourself follow the pack's, the newest first. Select a row to use it as the sound. Each recording keeps its own map points. Select Edit recordings… to move a recording to the other part (Full band or Backing) or remove it and its map points. Audio files stay on your device. They're included in backups and cloud sync unless you turn that off. Map the recording by tapping A map tells MajesticTab which bar of the tab plays at which time in the recording. The recording bar above the bar ruler shows the state of the map: Not mapped , Partly mapped , Mapped or Check bar with a bar number. Everything you do to map a recording starts there. In the recording bar, select the state, such as Not mapped . On a Guitar Pro tab, the Map sheet opens. In the Map sheet, select Tap along . Play the recording. Tap each bar of the tab when you hear it. Select Done . The Map sheet opens again and tells you whether the recording is mapped, and which bars to fix if it is not. On a PDF or text tab, selecting the state starts tapping straight away, and the recording bar has the controls for it. After you map a recording, the cursor follows it through tempo changes. The metronome and count-in follow it too. Mapping works for Guitar Pro, PDF and text tabs. The tap controls show play, back 5 and 10 seconds, speed, Undo and Done . More opens Fix range , the tap Offset , Calibrate , Snap for an audio file, Redo , Timeline and Edit points . Calibrate measures how long you take to tap after you hear a sound, and removes that delay from every tap. Correct map points When a recording has map points, select its state in the recording bar, such as Mapped , to open the Map sheet. It tells you what looks wrong: a bar whose point looks out of place, or bars with no point. From the sheet you can: Select Tap along again to tap over the bars that drift. In tap mode, select More and then Fix range to redo a stretch of bars. Select Edit points to open the points. There you can nudge a point, play two seconds around it to check it, move it to the nearest sound in the recording, shift every point at once, or delete a point. Reuse map points In the Map sheet, select Use another recording’s map to copy the points of another video or file of the same tab. If the other recording is an audio file and so is this one, MajesticTab lines them up by the sound. Otherwise it copies the times as they are. Then the points open so that you can shift them by ear. If this recording already has points, you select the other recording twice to replace them. Select Use another tab’s map to copy a mapped video from another tab of the same song. Select Import points… to load points from a file or an address. Add a backing track Switch the panel from Recording to Backing to attach a separate backing track to the same tab. Map it the same way. Then you can switch between the original recording and the backing track. To make the backing track follow the original recording’s points, turn on Use the original recording’s map in the Map sheet. Change the speed The original recording has its own speed options: 50%, 75%, 100% and 125%. Use a recording in a Jam Guests don't hear a local audio file from the host. They follow the host's YouTube video or the synth. See Jam sessions .

t: Fit a tab to your guitar
x: Show a Guitar Pro tab for the guitar you play. Every note keeps its pitch. The Guitar panel. Choose the number of strings Under Strings , select 6-String , Original , 7-String or 8-String . Original shows the tab as written. Match your tuning Under Tuning , you can choose from these options: Shift Frets moves the frets to match your tuning. Capo adapts the frets to a capo position that you set under Capo . Transpose keeps the same frets and retunes, so the song sounds lower or higher. When a tab is adapted to your guitar, the badge Adapted appears. Keep or discard your changes A change applies to the song that's open, and it resets when you close the song. To keep it, save it for that song or as your usual guitar. To set your starting string counts for new files, use Default strings under Player in Settings .

The reader's Tools menu opens the practice and reference tools while a score is open. The library has the same tools, and more, in its Tools view . The Tools menu. Show the fretboard On Guitar Pro tabs, the fretboard appears above the dock. It lights up the notes of the current beat, with a color for each track. To flip it for left-handed play, turn on Left-handed guitar under Player in Settings . To show or hide it, select Toggle fretboard in the dock, or press F . Open a tool Select Tools and then select a tool, or press its key: Tool Key What it does Chord library C Voicings for any tuning and capo Scales S Scales and modes on the neck Circle of fifths O Keys and their chords Tuner T Tune with the microphone Metronome M Keep time at any tempo Jam mode Host or join on your network

PDF and text tabs have their own reading tools. Many practice features work for them as they do for Guitar Pro tabs. Condense a PDF Multi-track Guitar Pro PDF exports often contain empty staves and wide margins. To remove them, turn on Condense PDF in the song menu. The option is marked Experimental . Bookmark pages In the song menu, select Bookmark Current Page to mark the page you're on. Select Bookmarks & Table of Contents to jump to your bookmarks or to the PDF's outline. Split a book into songs If one PDF contains a whole book, you can create songs from page ranges of it. Open the album that the book belongs to. Select Add book and choose where the PDF comes from. Select Set book pages and set the pages of each song. Turn pages PDF and text tabs have a page strip where Guitar Pro tabs have the bar ruler. You can turn pages by selecting either side of the page, with the arrow keys, or with a foot pedal. See The reader . Map to a recording You can map PDF and text tabs to a recording in the same way as Guitar Pro tabs. A recording bar shows the time and map state above the page strip. See Original recording . Export as PDF To export one tab, select Export as PDF in the song menu. To export your whole library, see Backup and sync .

In a Jam, one player hosts a session on the local network and the other players join from their own devices. Playback stays in sync, so everyone plays the same bar. Host a session Connect every device to the same network. Open Tools , select Jam mode , and then select Host a jam . Share the host address. Each address has a copy button and a QR code. Open a song. It opens for every player. Every MajesticTab app except the web version can host. To end the session, select Stop hosting . To remove one player, select Kick . A session holds up to 32 players. Join a session Open Tools , select Jam mode , and then select Join a jam . Scan the host's QR code or enter the host address. A player without the app can open the host address in a browser. What stays in sync Playback position. The host's YouTube video, including its map points. The song. Guitar Pro, PDF and text tabs all open for every player. The host's mixer settings and SoundFonts. A guest's device uses them during the session and returns to its own settings when the guest leaves. Assign tracks The host can assign each guitarist a part. A player can hear only their assigned tracks, or only the backing tracks. The host can also mute audio on guests, or mute assigned tracks for players who have no assignment. Know the limits A Jam works on a local network. It doesn't work over the internet. The host doesn't share local audio files. Guests hear the host's YouTube video or the synth.

x: The Tools view in the library lists every tool in one place: music reference, practice tools, tools for adding tabs, and tools for managing your library. Select a tool to open it. Open the Tools view In the library views at the top, select Tools . On a wide screen, the tool you select opens next to the list. On a phone, it replaces the list. The reader has its own Tools menu for the reference tools, the tuner, the metronome and Jam. See Fretboard and the Tools menu . Find a tool The list groups tools by purpose: Reference Chord library , Scales and Circle of fifths . Practice Tuner , Metronome and Jam . Getting tabs Open file , Classical tab browser and Fill in missing tabs . Library Bulk import and Bulk export . Some rows show a short note about the current state on the right. For example, Metronome shows the tempo, Classical tab browser shows how many pieces are installed, and Fill in missing tabs shows how many songs have no tab. The web version doesn't show it, but a browser can open a host's address to join. See Jam sessions .

h.t: Match the chords to your guitar

x: The chord library shows chord voicings that match your strings, tuning and capo. Open the chord library In the library, select Tools and then Chord library . In the reader, select Tools and then Chord library , or press C . Match the chords to your guitar The chord library uses the number of strings, the tuning and the capo that you set for the guitar in your hands. If you use 7 strings, a capo or a lower tuning, the chord diagrams change to match. In the Tools view, the row shows these settings. See Fit a tab to your guitar . Find a chord Use Chord view mode to choose how the chords are listed: Every chord type lists the chord types. Movable Shapes shows shapes that you can move along the neck. Each shape is drawn from its lowest fret. By Note shows the fingerings for the chord on the root note that you select. Select Prefer movable shapes to place movable shapes on that root instead. Select a root with Root note . Each chord type shows as a tile, and you can step through its shapes with the arrows. If no chord fits your filters, you see No chords match these filters. Change the diagram style Use Diagram orientation to choose Vertical diagrams (the traditional chord chart) or Horizontal diagrams (fretboard style). Hear a chord Select a chord name or its diagram to hear the chord strummed on a synthesized acoustic guitar.

h.t: Show a scale on the neck

x: Scales shows a scale or mode on a fretboard, so you can see where its notes fall on the neck. Open scales In the library, select Tools and then Scales . In the reader, select Tools and then Scales , or press S . Show a scale on the neck Select a Root note. Select a Scale or mode , for example Major Pentatonic or Minor Pentatonic . Set the Strings and the Tuning to match your guitar. The Interactive Scale Fretboard marks the notes of the scale. The root note is marked in the main text color. Scale degrees 2 to 7 each take one of the six guitar track colors. The Formula shows how the scale is built.

The circle of fifths shows how keys relate to each other, and the chords in each key. Open the circle of fifths In the library, select Tools and then Circle of fifths . In the reader, select Tools and then Circle of fifths , or press O . Look up a key Select a key on the circle. MajesticTab shows these details for it: Key signature Relative minor Chords in the key of the key you selected

The tuner listens to your guitar through the microphone and shows how far each note is from the pitch you want. Tune your guitar Open the tuner. In the library, select Tools and then Tuner . In the reader, select Tools and then Tuner , or press T . Select Start tuner . If your device asks, allow microphone access. The tuner needs the microphone to listen to your instrument. Play one string. The tuner shows the note and whether it is sharp or flat, in cents. Before you play, the tuner shows Waiting for audio . If the microphone isn't available, you see Microphone access failed . Choose what to tune Choose a number of Strings . Choose one of your Library tunings . While a tab is open, choose the Active track to tune to that track's tuning. Choose chromatic mode to detect every note on any instrument. It detects every note in any pitch range. Hear a reference note Select Play a note to hear the pitch you are tuning to. Set the reference pitch To change the pitch that the tuner uses for A4, use the Reference pitch for A4 control.

h.t: Use the metronome while you practice

x: The metronome keeps time at any tempo. It has a tempo display, tap tempo and time signatures. Start the metronome Open the metronome. In the library, select Tools and then Metronome . In the reader, select Tools and then Metronome , or press M . Set the tempo. Select − or + , type digits, or use the arrow keys. Hold Shift with the arrow keys to change the tempo in steps of 10. Select Start . To start or stop from a keyboard, press Space . Set the tempo by tapping Select Tap tempo in time with the music. On a keyboard, press T . Change the time signature Use Time signature and how many bars to play it to set a time signature and how long it lasts. Select Add another time signature to play a sequence of them. Select Reset to 4/4 to start again. Change how the click shows Mute the click keeps the display and silences the sound. From a keyboard, press M . Blink on the beat flashes the dot above the arm. Use the metronome while you practice The Metronome and Count-in switches in Practice are separate from this tool. See Practice .

h.t: Search the web for a tab
Open a file from cloud storage

x: Open file plays a tab without adding it to your library. Open a file In the library, select Tools and then Open file . On the start screen of an empty library, select Open a single file . Select Browse files and choose a file. In the web app and on Mac and Windows you can also drop a tab file on the page. The page opens Guitar Pro files, PDFs and text tabs. See Supported files . Search the web for a tab Enter a song in the search field Search the web for a tab… and select Search . Searching the web needs an internet connection. Open a file from cloud storage Under Or open from , select a storage provider that you connected, such as Google Drive, S3, WebDAV or iCloud, to browse its folders. See Getting tabs in . Keep the tab To add the open tab to your library, open the song menu in the reader and select Save to library .

h.t: Add a piece to your library

x: The classical tab browser lets you search and open classical guitar tabs and MIDI files. The tabs come from Classtab , a free archive of classical guitar tabs. You download the archive once. After that, it works offline. About Classtab Classtab ( classtab.org ) publishes the classical guitar tabs and MIDI files that this browser shows. MajesticTab doesn't include or host them. You download the archive from classtab.org, and MajesticTab reads the pieces from the copy on your device. To learn more about the archive or its sources, visit the Classtab website . Download the archive The first time you open the browser, it offers the archive of about 3,800 pieces by 600 composers. Choose one of these: Select Download archive . MajesticTab downloads it once from classtab.org. In the apps, the download is about 14 MB. Select Use a ZIP from this device and then Choose ZIP file if you already have the archive. If you can't download from inside the app, get the archive from classtab.org and use Use a ZIP from this device . Open the classical tab browser In the library, select Tools and then Classical tab browser . On the start screen of an empty library, select Explore classical guitar library . Find a piece Select a composer in the Composers list to see their pieces. On a phone, the browser shows one list at a time. Type in Search composers and pieces to search both. Use the filters to narrow the list. Select Clear filters to remove them. Open Pinned to see the pieces you pinned. Select a piece to open it. MajesticTab reads the piece from the stored archive. Add a piece to your library A piece that you added shows In your library . To add it again, select Add another copy . Pieces in your library are copies. They stay when you remove the archive. Thank you, Classtab. Classtab gives guitarists free access to about 3,800 pieces by 600 composers, as tabs and MIDI files. That is a large body of classical repertoire that anyone can learn from, practice with and play, at no cost. Many guitarists rely on it, and we are grateful to the people who built and maintain it. If you find it useful, visit classtab.org and support their work.

Fill in missing tabs lists the songs in your library that have no tab. For each song, you can search the web for one. Check what you need This tool is in the MajesticTab apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. On the web, you add tabs to a song one at a time. See Getting tabs in . Fill in missing tabs In the library, select Tools and then Fill in missing tabs . To work on one artist, choose the artist in Artist . The default is All artists . Select Search on a song to search the web for it. Download the tab file. If it does not open in MajesticTab on its own, select Add tab on the song and choose the file. The page shows how many songs have no tab. If every song has one, you see Every song in your library has a tab. To copy or save the list of songs, select Copy list or Export list .

h.t: Skip songs that have a tab

x: Bulk import adds many files at once. You choose a folder, and MajesticTab pairs each file with a song. You review the pairings before anything is imported. Open Bulk import In the library, select Tools and then Bulk import . On the start screen of an empty library, select Bulk import a folder of tabs . Importing a folder needs the MajesticTab app on a computer, or the Chrome or Edge browser. On a phone, add tabs to a song one at a time. Import a folder of tabs Select Tabs at the top of the page. Select Choose folder and choose the folder. MajesticTab includes subfolders. Under Pair by , choose how your files are named. See the next section. Review the list. Each row shows the song that the file is paired with. Clear the check box on a file to leave it out. Select Import . MajesticTab reads Guitar Pro, PDF and text files. If the folder has none, you see No Guitar Pro, PDF or text files were found in that folder. Choose how files are named Under Pair by , choose one of these: Automatic picks the best reading for each file. Artist - Song reads names like Artist - Song.gp5 . Artist/Album/Song reads folders like Artist/Album/03 Song.gp5 . A track number before the song is ignored. Automatic can also use the title, artist and album written inside a Guitar Pro file. PDF and text files don't carry that information. Fix a pairing MajesticTab looks each pairing up in your library and then on MusicBrainz. The rows fill in while the lookups run. You can change any row: Select Search to find the song or album on MusicBrainz. Select Use as custom music to import the file under the names you type. Clear the check box to leave the file out. Use the switch Import files with no good match as custom music to save songs that MusicBrainz can't find, or only guesses at, under the names from the file. Import a tab book A PDF that is a whole album's tab book can be paired with an album instead of a song. For each file, choose One song or A whole album's tab book under This file is . If the album isn't on MusicBrainz, select Use as custom album tab . Skip songs that have a tab The switch Skip songs and albums that already have a tab leaves out a file when its song, or its album's tab book, already has a tab. To import that file anyway, check its row. Import audio files Select Audio files at the top of the page to match a folder of audio files to songs that are already in your library and have a tab. A file with no matching song is left out. Under The files are , choose what each file becomes: Automatic makes each file the song's original recording, unless its name says "backing track" or "no guitar". Then it becomes the backing track. Recordings of the songs makes every file the song's original recording. Backing tracks makes every file the song's backing track. If a match is a guess, check it. To pick a different song, use Search your library for this song . On a phone, add audio to a song from its Sound panel instead.

Bulk export saves your whole library in one of four forms: a spreadsheet, your map points, your original tab files or printable PDFs. Open Bulk export In the library, select Tools and then Bulk export . Export your library Under Bulk export modes , choose a mode. Select the export button for that mode. When the export is ready, select Save / Share to save or share the file. While an export runs, the page shows its progress. Select Cancel to stop it. Choose a mode Library metadata Select Export metadata as CSV . The CSV spreadsheet has these columns: artist, album, song, YouTube URL, YouTube backing URL, tunings, tab files and year. Map data Select Export map data as ZIP . The ZIP has one JSON file for each song and recording, in artist and album folders. Each file names the YouTube video or audio file that the map points belong to. Original tab files Select Export original tabs as ZIP . The ZIP has the .gp , .pdf and .txt files from your library and storage. Select Include unlinked tab files from storage to add files that no song uses. They go in an Unsorted folder. PDF export Select Export all tabs as PDF (ZIP) . MajesticTab lays out every tab in your library and exports each as a printable A4 PDF. The ZIP has artist and album folders. If your library has nothing to export, you see a message such as No tab files found .

Keyboard shortcuts work while a score is open and no text field has focus. The same list is in the app. Open Settings and select Controls . Control playback These keys control playback and the setlist: Key Action Space Play or pause. If no audio is loaded, go to the next page. B Go back 10 seconds G Switch between full band and no guitars (no bass, in bass mode) M Turn the metronome on or off I Turn the count-in on or off , . Slow down or speed up by 5% [ ] Open the previous or next tab in the open setlist Open panels These keys open and close panels: Key Action F Show or hide the fretboard T Show or hide the tuner C Show or hide the chord library S Show or hide the scales O Show or hide the circle of fifths R Turn Reading mode on or off Esc Close the open dialog, menu or panel Turn pages and navigate These keys and mouse buttons turn pages and move through the app: Key Action → ↓ Page Down Next page, or scroll down in scroll mode ← ↑ Page Up Previous page, or scroll up in scroll mode Click the right or left half of the page Next or previous page Cmd [ , Alt ← or Mouse 4 Back Cmd ] , Alt → or Mouse 5 Forward Arrow keys and Enter In the library, move between items and open a tab Zoom and full screen These shortcuts change the zoom and the screen mode: Key Action Ctrl and the mouse wheel, or a pinch Zoom the score between 50% and 150% Mouse wheel in scroll mode Scroll the score Alt Enter Turn full screen on or off (Windows and Linux)

You can turn pages and control playback without touching the screen. MajesticTab supports Bluetooth foot pedals and game controllers. Use a Bluetooth foot pedal MajesticTab works with AirTurn, PageFlip and Donner pedals. Most page-turn pedals connect as a Bluetooth keyboard and send arrow or page keys. MajesticTab treats those keys like the keys in Keyboard shortcuts . Pair the pedal in your device's Bluetooth settings. Then open a tab and press the pedal. Use a game controller MajesticTab supports Xbox, PlayStation and Steam Deck controllers. To see the controller diagram, open Settings , select Controls , and then select Game Controller . While a score is open, the controls work as follows: Control Action A Play or pause X Go back 10 seconds, or one measure B Return to the library Y Toggle Reading mode LB or LT Previous page RB or RT Next page Left stick Scroll smoothly Right stick Zoom in and out Left or right stick click Change the view mode, or reset the zoom to 100% In the library and in menus, the controls work as follows: Control Action A Select, or open the selected tab B Go back, or close a dialog X Focus the search field Y Show or hide the top bar D-pad or left stick Move the focus Right stick, vertical Scroll a list LB or RB Previous or next library tab View button Cycle the audio. Hold to show the controller guide.

Settings contains the defaults that MajesticTab starts from, plus your cloud sync and data tools. Some options only appear in the apps. Open Settings Select Settings in the library navigation. Settings has these sections: Cloud sync , Data management , Player , Appearance , Reading , Controls , Sound , Updates and About . The apps also have Web search . In the reader, View and Guitar override some of these defaults for the song that is open. Cloud sync Sync with cloud storage Keeps this device and your backup location matching. Select Sync . See Backup and sync . Auto-sync cloud storage Keeps your library synced in the background when a location is connected. Keep all files on device Downloads every song in your library during sync. Data management Create a backup Saves everything to a file, a folder or your cloud. Select Create . Restore from a backup Brings a backup or snapshot back. Select Restore . Reload library metadata Refreshes covers, durations and album details. Select Reload . Orphaned files Finds stored tabs that no library song uses. Select Review . Clear cached data Clears covers and downloads that MajesticTab keeps only to load faster. Select Clear . Delete all data Removes your library, setlists and settings from this device. Select Delete . Make a backup first. The Classical tab group manages the Classtab archive for the classical tab browser . After you download the archive, it shows its size and how many pieces and composers it holds. Select Update archive to download it again, or Remove to delete it. Songs that you added to your library stay. The archive isn't part of your backup, so you can download it again at any time. Player Preferred instrument Choose Guitar or Bass . This sets the instrument that MajesticTab assumes. Left-handed guitar Flips the fretboard and the chord diagrams for a left-handed guitar. Stringing Standard puts the high string on top, as in tab. Upside down puts the low string on top. Default strings For guitar, choose From file , 7 or 8 . For bass, choose From file , 5 or 6 . From file keeps the string count that the tab was saved with. Appearance Under App theme , choose one of nine themes: Slate Blue, Mystic Dream, Blue Pearl, Cerulean Paradise, Dark Side, Ember Glow, Purple Nebula, Red Nebula or Snow White. Under Library , Hide songs without tabs shows only songs that have at least one tab. Reading A new tab opens as Choose Page or Scroll separately for Guitar Pro, PDF and text files. Notation Choose Tab only or Tab and standard for a new tab. To change it for one song, use View . Reset these defaults Select Reset to return to Scroll for Guitar Pro and text files, Page for PDFs, and string counts from the file. Minimum section size Choose 1 bar , 2 bars , 4 bars or 8 bars . MajesticTab joins shorter labeled sections with adjacent parts. Size, paper and the pages shown are in the reader's View menu, not in Settings. Controls Shows what each key, foot pedal or controller button does. See Keyboard shortcuts and Foot pedals and game controllers . Web search Under Default search provider , choose the site or search engine that opens first when you search for a tab. Select Add custom search provider to add another. Use $s where the song and artist go in its address. Select Reset search providers to restore the defaults. Sound SoundFonts Select Add to add a SoundFont and Edit to change the list. Enabled SoundFonts layer from top to bottom, and lower ones override higher ones. Strict instrument matching Tracks that the enabled SoundFonts lack stay silent. Force one preset Plays every instrument except drums with a single preset from one SoundFont. The default is Off (use each track's instrument) . Updates This section appears in versions that update themselves. Under Update channel , choose None , Canary or Stable . None turns automatic checks off. Canary gets early builds. Select Check next to Check for updates to look for a newer version now. About The About section has these rows: User guide opens this guide. Privacy policy opens the privacy policy . Support opens the issue tracker, where you can report a problem or ask for a feature. Quit closes MajesticTab in versions that can quit.

This page lists the file types that MajesticTab opens and creates. Tab files you can open MajesticTab opens these types of tab: Type Extensions Guitar Pro .gp , .gp3 , .gp4 , .gp5 , .gpx PDF .pdf Text tab .txt Audio For the original recording, you can use a YouTube video or an audio file on your device. For the synth, you can add SoundFonts in .sf2 and .sf3 format. Files MajesticTab creates File Contents .mtbackup Your library, settings and SoundFonts .mpak A single song .pdf One exported tab. Bulk Export saves many PDFs in one ZIP archive.

x: This page answers common questions and lists fixes for common problems. If your problem isn't here, open an issue on GitHub . Common questions Does MajesticTab work offline? Yes. The built-in synth plays tabs without a connection. YouTube, web search, the music catalog and cloud sync need the internet. You choose whether to use them. Does MajesticTab have subscriptions or locked features? No. MajesticTab has no subscriptions, in-app purchases, ads or trial periods. On the Apple App Store, a one-time purchase unlocks the app on iPhone, iPad and Mac. Where does MajesticTab store my tabs? On your device, unless you back them up or sync them. See Backup and sync . How does MajesticTab help if I play a 7-string or 8-string guitar? You can show a Guitar Pro tab on 7 or 8 strings, or move the frets to match your tuning, with a capo or transposed. Every note keeps its pitch. To start new files on 7 or 8 strings, set Default strings under Player in Settings . See Fit a tab to your guitar . Fix sound that plays late If you use a Bluetooth speaker or headphones, open Sound and set Audio latency , or select Calibrate . See Sound . Fix a cursor that drifts from the recording In the recording bar, select the state of the recording, such as Mapped . The Map sheet shows which bars to check. Select Tap along again to tap over the bars where the cursor drifts, or select Edit points to nudge a single point. See Original recording . Fix a wrong album cover or a missing tracklist Open Settings , select Data management , and then select Reload next to Reload library metadata . Check your internet connection if the catalog doesn't respond. Fix a pedal that doesn't turn pages Check that the pedal is paired in your device's Bluetooth settings. If the pedal has a key setting, set it to send arrow keys. See Foot pedals and game controllers . Fix a Jam that you can't join Both devices must be on the same network. Some guest and public Wi-Fi networks stop devices from reaching each other. Use a private network or a phone hotspot instead. Recover a library that disappeared in the browser Browsers can clear site storage. Restore your library from a .mtbackup file. To prevent this, make regular backups or use cloud sync . Report a problem Open an issue on GitHub . Include what you did, what you expected, your platform and the app version.
